flagging._note: Flags compare each move with what this page has already seen for that item and for its comparison group, so thresholds are multiples of normal range, not fixed percentages. Priors are starting guesses for daily volatility (percent, or percentage points for yields) and fade as real observations accumulate. See scripts/compute_flags.py and README.md.

reading.coverage_rule: No filtering for quality or fit. Take up to max_items_per_feed from every enabled feed that has items in the window, newest first, then stop at max_items_total. Do not drop an item for being off-theme; set overlap to empty instead.

headlines.rule: Pick the biggest announcements of the period: policy and trade decisions, export controls, central bank decisions, major production or capacity moves, large company news, and disruptions to supply. For each story cite 2 to 4 outlets from at least 2 different regions when the story is covered that way, and always include one outlet from the region the story concerns. Add one official or primary source (agency, exchange, company release) with kind set to primary when it exists. Use the outlet's own headline wording. Fill framing only when headlines or emphasis visibly differ, describe the difference neutrally in under 25 words, and never judge which outlet is right. Do not let one wire service count as several outlets. Paywalled outlets: use only the visible headline and snippet.
headlines.outlet_pool_note: A starting pool, not a limit. Runs may use any reputable outlet. Spread across regions so no country's press is the default.

quality._note: Every priced item carries a source tier. Flagged items and a rotating audit sample get a second, independent source. See scripts/check_quality.py and README.md.

tiers.official: the issuing body's own page: an exchange, central bank, agency, company investor page, or trade association
tiers.reported: a news report quoting an official release, not the release itself
tiers.aggregator: a quote or data site that compiles numbers from elsewhere

quality.rule: A second source must be independent of the first (a different issuer, not a mirror) and show the same trading date. If the dates differ, record as_of on the second source and leave status to the script.

indicators._note: Operational series for the chip equipment and memory chain. Each lives in data/series/<id>.csv, append-only, with revisions kept as new rows. Release timing: lag_months counts from the period's end month, release_day is the usual day of that month. Backfills were read from official releases.

series.name: TSMC monthly revenue
series.note: Consolidated revenue, issued about the 10th. Year-to-date is recorded so months can be reconciled against it.

series.name: Korea semiconductor exports
series.find: Korea <Month> <Year> exports semiconductor exports billion year-on-year ministry release
series.note: Released on the 1st. Mostly read from news reports of the ministry release unless the release itself is found; the ministry's English name changes between outlets.

series.name: Japan-made chip equipment billings
series.note: Semiconductor equipment only. SEAJ also publishes flat panel display equipment with a near-identical title; do not use that report. Figures are 3-month averages, and the first release of a month is preliminary.

series.name: Global chip equipment billings
series.find: SEMI Reports Global Semiconductor Equipment Billings <Quarter> <Year>
series.note: Quarterly, released about three months after the quarter ends. Regional tables are images, so only the global total is recorded.

series.name: Global semiconductor sales
series.find: SIA global semiconductor sales <Month> <Year> three-month moving average
series.note: 3-month moving average of monthly sales. Earlier months are revised in later releases, so revisions are stored as new rows.

series.name: FAO Food Price Index
series.note: Published the first Friday of the month on fao.org. The previous month is often revised, so enter any restated value again.

series.name: FAO cereals sub-index
series.note: Same FAO release as the headline index.

series.name: FAO vegetable oils sub-index
series.find: FAO Food Price Index <Month> <Year> vegetable oils
series.note: Same FAO release as the headline index.

series.name: FAO sugar sub-index
series.note: Same FAO release as the headline index.

series.name: US corn ending stocks, 2026/27 projection
series.note: World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates, about the 10th. The projected marketing year rolls over each September, so month-on-month change compares like with like only within a year.

series.name: US rotary rig count (Baker Hughes)
series.find: Baker Hughes rig count <Week> US total
series.note: Published Fridays. The release is reached through press reports quoting Baker Hughes, so tier stays reported unless the Baker Hughes page itself is reachable.

series.name: US working gas in storage (EIA)
series.find: EIA weekly natural gas storage report week ending <Week>
series.note: Thursday release for the week ending the prior Friday. The EIA page can return an old cached copy: check that its week-ending date matches the period before recording a value.

series.name: EU gas storage, percent full (GIE)
series.find: Gas Infrastructure Europe EU gas storage percent full <Week>
series.note: Reached through press reports quoting GIE until the AGSI+ page itself is reachable. Use the Sunday figure.

series.name: Refined copper market balance, year to date (ICSG)
series.find: ICSG refined copper balance <Month> <Year> surplus deficit
series.note: Positive is surplus, negative is deficit, cumulative within the year. Reached through press reports quoting ICSG.

spreads._note: Computed from prices already on the page. Each is a relationship between two markets, shown against its own recent sessions.

list.name: Brent minus WTI
list.note: Gap between the two main crude benchmarks.

list.name: Copper to aluminum price ratio
list.note: Copper in USD per tonne (pounds converted) divided by aluminum in USD per tonne.

list.name: Copper to gold ratio
list.note: Copper USD per pound divided by gold USD per ounce, times 1000. A familiar growth-versus-safety gauge.
